set.body:
The highest-leverage change in the epic, and the one that needs no cache
policy or invalidation design.

`PlotCompiler.compile` runs mapping -> stats -> scale training -> row
resolution -> coord -> layout solve -> geom lowering -> guide lowering ->
device lowering (`PlotCompiler.scala:428-460`). Only the phases from the
layout solve onward consume `RenderContext`/`LayoutPolicy`. Yet
`PlotCompiler.resolve` just sets `options.renderContext`
(`PlotCompiler.scala:398-402`) and `effectiveOptions` rebuilds the policy
(`:404-426`), so the whole thing re-runs.

Consequence today: dragging a splitter recomputes histogram bins, density
kernels, summary intervals (`Stats.scala`) and discrete/continuous scale
domains, none of which can have changed.

Proposal: make the intermediate value public and stable so the surface
becomes roughly

    Plot[Row]              --train-->  TrainedPlot      (data-dependent)
    TrainedPlot + Context  --place-->  ResolvedPlot     (device-dependent)

with `resolve(plot, context)` preserved as the composition so no consumer
breaks. A resize then calls `place` alone. `TrainedPlot` already exists
(`PlotCompiler.scala:160-167`) and may be the right cut as it stands.

Constraints to respect:

- Faceting trains a global registry plus per-panel registries
  (`FacetCompiler.scala:29-115`); both belong on the data side.
- Free scales retrain per panel but still only on data, not device.
- Layout measurement uses `LayoutPolicy.metrics` (`FacetCompiler.scala:220-229`),
  which is device-side and must stay there.
- Purity and determinism must hold: `place` twice at one context yields
  identical scenes.

Acceptance: the `resize-only` workload shows zero stat-phase and zero
scale-training time on every resize after the first, with byte-identical
output to a full recompile at the same size.
set.title: Split the compile pipeline at the data/device seam so a resize does no statistical work
